title: The belt-buckle moves and the null-homotopy of distinct twist types on a fold
author: Hank Chen
work: Categorical quantum symmetries and ribbon tensor 2-categories
difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is not a formal consequence of the definitions that precede it. Even with the rigid dagger tensor 2-category, its folds, its ribbon balancings and the quasi-Hermitian hypothesis on the braiding all available as context, the author has to construct the two belt-buckle 2-morphisms P and Q explicitly: the first is built as a large pasting diagram whose central triangle is filled by a braided composite and whose right-hand square is a coherence 2-morphism of the evaluation, and the second is obtained by the mirror construction. The proposition is then proved by exhibiting an explicit chain of 2-morphisms that drags a twist from the outside of a fold to the top, applies P, transports the twist across the fold with a braiding coherence, applies Q, and closes with the cancellation of a 2-morphism against its own adjoint coming from quasi-Hermiticity. Building that chain, and checking that each step is a well-formed 2-morphism between the required composites, is research-level work in the higher category theory of ribbon tensor 2-categories, far beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
